text:
alex.k: FYI I'm landing a refactor that hoists provider blocks to the root and replaces in-module provider declarations with provider_aliases. Local `terraform plan` looks ok but I hit one weird diff related to a secrets connector resource. opening PR now :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria_g: tagging—please add a short summary in the PR description about: state impact, lockfile regen, and any manual steps for on-prem private tenants. QA will need that. :+1:

samir: can you paste the small plan snippet where the connector resource changed? curious if it's a provider_change or a forced-recreate.

alex.k: pasted plan excerpt from my workspace: ```
-/+ module.alpha.module.secret_connector.null_resource.secrets (known after apply)
  ~ resource "null_resource" "secrets" {
      - triggers = {
          - "version" = "v1" -> null
        } -> null
    }
```
This came from moving provider config; looks like a meta-attribute that used an interpolated provider addr. Not an actual secret rotation but terraform thinks it's a replace.

lina_ops: hmm could be a subtle provider meta-attribute that includes provider config hash. In past refactors we've avoided noise by:
- regenerate .terraform.lock.hcl (lockfile)
- run `terraform state replace-provider` where module resource provider addresses changed

alex.k: yeah my plan was: 1) hoist providers, 2) run `terraform init -upgrade` to refresh lockfile, 3) run `terraform state replace-provider` for the affected module path, 4) apply in staging, smoke test secrets wiring.

maria_g: +1. Please add the exact `replace-provider` command to the PR so SRE can run it with the right addresses. Example format: ```
terraform state replace-provider 
  'module.alpha.module.secret_connector.provider["registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws"]' 
  'registry.terraform.io/custom/providers/aws@~> 4.0'
```

samir: also call out that Dedicated customers on older provider versions may need a small migration window. If you can, include a short rollback plan (how to re-pin to old provider and revert state replace).

alex.k: will do. quick question: do we want to include a lockfile regen commit in the same PR or land it separately? pros/cons?

lina_ops: I'd prefer separate commit in same PR: keeps history but shows regen context. CI will re-run and catch any provider-compat diffs. If CI passes, merge. If not, revert the regen commit and iterate.

infra-bot: CI: plan job triggered for PR #8273 — plan completed with 2 warnings (provider lockfile change, module address changes). See link: https://ci.internal/8273/plan

maria_g: thanks. alex, once you push the commands and notes we can do a brief pairing session for the state replace in staging. I'll book 15m after the PR is green.

alex.k: thanks all — pushing updates now. will @maria_g when ready for pairing. :rocket:
